instructions.question: Does the tweet lean positive or negative in feeling, or is it truly neutral with no emotional lean?
instructions.rule: Choose neutral only when the tweet has no emotional lean: plain information, dry ads or listings, stats, questions, or jokes with no complaint or delight. If a personal tweet leans even mildly pleasant (looking forward to a treat, trip, show or outing; liking something; warm tributes), choose positive. If it leans even mildly unpleasant (letdowns, sighs like 'dang it' or 'Argh', digs at someone, sadness, bad outcomes), choose negative. For news-style tweets, clear successes are positive and clear harm (deaths, injuries, violence, charges, delays, disputes) is negative.

neutral.what: Purely informational or flat tweets: ads, schedules, stats, scores, headlines without clear good or bad outcome, questions, and remarks with no detectable feeling.
examples: Anyone wanna buy a Zac Brown Band ticket for the 3rd?
Get ready for our Wednesday Drink Specials Wednesday - 3-8pm Have it your Way Margarita Day  ( Bar Brand Only)...
David Wright is 6 for 20 with 5 walks in five games with St. Lucie.
neutral.cues: selling, tickets, reminder, specials, scheduled, reportedly, 'may' speculation, game stats, dates
neutral.not_for: Personal tweets with any pleasant lean (positive) or any letdown, sigh or dig (negative).

positive.what: Any mild or strong pleasant lean: anticipation of plans or treats, enjoyment, liking, praise, pride, affection, tributes, or news of a clear success.
examples: I want IHOP tomorrow morning
In the car on our way to Milton Keynes to see the Foo Fighters tomorrow. #foofighters #miltonkeynes
8th strikeout of the afternoon for David Price's 100th career win!
Sending my sincere prayers & condolences to the Gifford family on Frank Gifford's passing. May he rest in peace.
positive.cues: want, can't wait, going to see, love, glad, fun, excited, proud, wins, tops, honored, :), !
positive.not_for: Dry ads, ticket sales or event listings with no personal enthusiasm (neutral).

negative.what: Any mild or strong unpleasant lean: letdowns, frustration, sadness, envy, insults, mockery, fear, or news of clear harm or failure.
examples: Might not be able to get a free taco tomorrow. As Napoleon Dynamite would say, dang it!
Just remembered I'm taking the PSSAs tomorrow. #Fml
RT @user Gavin Henson looks set to miss the Rugby World Cup after dislocating a bone in his right wrist yesterday
negative.cues: dang it, Argh, why oh why, sad, can't, not happy, worst, sucks, hate, #Fml, injured, delayed, killed
negative.not_for: Flat factual reports with no bad outcome (neutral); tributes expressing warmth (positive).
